text:
Maria G.: Heads up — profiler on nightly canary shows tail-latency spikes when prefetch sampler is enabled. FlashAttention path seems to sometimes fallback to generic kernel mid-batch.
perf-bot: nightly/canary #482: p99 latency +120ms (7% reg), changed since 1932090000.
Ashwin P.: can you paste the flame graph? also which model/config?
Maria G.: running 13B, seq=1024, token_budget_target=5000, sampler=slot-prefetch, paged_kv=on
Devon K.: quick logs from the worker reproduced locally:
```
worker0: kernel_switch: flash->fallback at token=384, queued=8, batch_sz=6
worker0: kv_page_faults=2, prefetch_hits=1
```
Anita R.: interesting — page faults cause stalls, kernel swap happens because attention kernel path expects contiguous KV; paged-kv page faults force a copy/merge that invalidates fast path.
Leo T.: maybe sampler prefetch size too small; it leaves hole for paged KV to trigger. also our kernel selector currently uses batch token estimate + contiguous_kv_hint, might be fragile.
Ashwin P.: try bumping prefetch_window to 768 and reduce token_budget_target to 4200 for a probe run.
Maria G.: testing now, running microbenchmark with `./perf/run_batcher --canary --prefetch 768 --budget 4200`
perf-bot: perf/job/19321 complete: p99 down 45ms vs canary baseline, cpu kernel time reduced, kv_page_faults -> 0 in 99.3% of batches.
Devon K.: results look promising but saw one outlier where batcher fused small seqs into large microbatch causing kernel coercion mid-batch (small->large seq changed attention plan).
Maria G.: added instrumentation PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/runtime/pulls/782 — collects per-batch kernel_id, estimated_token_budget, and kv_page_events.
Anita R.: can we add a safety-latch: if kv_page_faults>1 within batch -> force paged-kv fallback path earlier to avoid mid-batch kernel swap? that would avoid tail spikes at cost of a slower path for that batch.
Leo T.: +1. Also add metric: prefetch_hit_rate per-token and kernel_swap_count per-batch. We'll need dashboards.
Ashwin P.: I'll own the canary. rolling flag `batcher.prefetch_probe_v2` to 10% now. monitor p99, kernel_swap_count, prefetch_hit_rate, kv_page_faults.
Maria G.: plan: roll 10% -> if p99 and kernel_swap_count stable at baseline -> roll to 50% -> iterate prefetch size and token_budget targets. I'll post periodic perf dumps in thread.
perf-bot: action items created: PERF-314 (add kernel_swap_count metric), PERF-315 (safety-latch for paged-kv).
Maria G.: thanks — tagging @Ashwin P. for follow-up, will post summarized findings in eng-runtime weekly.
